newsitem.title: USA: Teachers point to parents for educational problems.
newsitem.headline: Teachers point to parents for educational problems.

text.p: Most top schoolteachers believe parents are uninvolved in their children's lives and that student apathy poses the gravest threat to the U.S. educational system, according to a survey released Tuesday.
The survey of 2,700 teachers by the publisher of "Who's Who Among America's Teachers" presented what it called "a disturbing picture of weak schools, disengaged parents and unmotivated youth."

Nearly three-quarters of the teachers, most with a decade of classroom experience, who had been picked for their excellence by the best students, said parents today were "less willing or able to spend time with their children." A majority of the teachers also said parents were less involved in their children's lives and were less ethical and moral.
"If parents are alienated from their children's lives, how can we expect young people to develop the kind of values that will help them succeed in school and adult life?" publisher Paul Krouse asked.

Only one-third of the teachers thought their schools were excellent, and just 27 percent thought students were being challenged academically. The biggest threats to schools were, in order of importance, unmotivated students, school funding, drugs and alcohol, violence and discipline and racial problems, the teachers said.

More than four out of five of the teachers surveyed said today's students were less respectful of authority. Between half and two-thirds thought children had become less ethical, less responsible, less studious and more self-centred.

While about half of both teachers and their pupils were aware that students cheated on their schoolwork and had problems with alcohol, only a small proportion of parents realised these problems existed, the survey found.

"This is role modelling from hell," Krouse said. "Since this is the first generation of parents that acknowledge experimentation with drugs, they apparently think it is inevitable or of little concern that teen drinking is so widespread."
